PullRequest.Title: mcp: add gated workspace-root configuration entry points
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Allow new nongallery workspace-folder MCP servers to use `.mcp.json` without replacing existing `.vscode/mcp.json` configurations.

- Add the experimental, default-off `chat.mcp.workspaceRootConfig.enabled` setting. When enabled, new folder additions use root configuration directly unless a legacy file exists, in which case users choose the destination.
- Make **Open Workspace Folder MCP Configuration** offer a file picker only when both files exist; open the sole existing file directly regardless of the new-add setting.
- Preserve explicit editor targets and add per-folder choices for multi-root additions while retaining global, remote-user, aggregate workspace, and current-session behavior.
- Keep gallery installations on supported legacy targets. Nongallery installation links follow the same root/legacy rules as manual additions.
- Show actionable failure notifications, keep cancellation silent, and shorten incompatible-root guidance in the destination picker.

## Implementation notes

Root files use `mcpServers`, with guarded edits preserving existing wrapped/flat JSONC content. Unsupported inputs, interpolation, and metadata are rejected rather than silently dropped or written elsewhere. No automatic migration is performed.

Manage both configuration sources using exact resource/server identity. Preserve independent root runtime discovery, exclude root inventory before legacy name precedence, and retain root provenance when runtime discovery is unavailable. Same-name root entries must not substitute for gallery results, and a successful first installation updates the already-open details editor.

The commits are ordered for review: root format/persistence, dual-source lifecycle/discovery, gated entry points, gallery/editor integration fixes, then notification and wording follow-ups. Each layer includes focused tests.

## Validation

- Before the notification/copy follow-ups: 178 targeted unit tests, client typecheck, layer checks, and targeted ESLint passed.
- Real Code OSS 1.138.0 Dev validation on macOS arm64: 75 scenario steps passed across file/setting matrices, multi-root routing, JSONC preservation, same-name lifecycle, chat entry points, local MCP tool discovery, access/reload behavior, and gallery/raw-URI installation. Gallery tests used a loopback mock registry rather than the production marketplace.
- That UI run found missing error feedback for an unsupported root-editor addition. The notification follow-up addresses it; client typecheck and targeted lint passed. Runtime revalidation of the notification/copy follow-ups was blocked by the local sandbox/Electron test-launch environment.
- The final concise-message change passed 13 Node-runner configuration tests, targeted lint, and editor diagnostics.

Signed-in Agent Host/model invocation, remote targets, production-gallery authentication, and VoiceOver speech were not exercised. Kept as a draft for review and CI validation.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added per-folder call, its awaited startup path, the unconditional scan/watch lifecycle, and the pre-existing independent root discovery read/watch are all directly traced in repository code. Exact remote latency and typical folder count vary, which affects severity but not the duplicated F-scaling mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: filesystem reads, provider watch subscriptions, and file-change listener CPU work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For F workspace folders, this adds F eager `readFile` attempts and F long-lived uncorrelated file watches/listeners; the additions are launched together through `Promise.allSettled`, so remote workspaces receive an F-wide startup burst, and subsequent filesystem events are checked by F extra listeners.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased MCP readiness/startup latency in large or remote multi-root workspaces, plus persistent filesystem watcher and event-dispatch overhead
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Workspace management eagerly created services only for the workspace and each folder's `.vscode/mcp.json`. Workspace-root `.mcp.json` already had its own `WorkspaceDotMcpDiscovery` path, which performs an initial read and owns a correlated watcher for each folder after restore.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added call creates a second management service for every folder's `.mcp.json`, even when the file does not exist. `addWorkspaceService` awaits `service.getInstalled()`, which reads the file, and `AbstractMcpResourceManagementService.initialize()` then always calls `fileService.watch` and registers a global `onDidFilesChange` listener for that same resource.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added RIGHT-side call at line 643 invokes `addWorkspaceService(...WORKSPACE_ROOT_MCP_CONFIG_FILE...)` for every added/initial workspace folder. That transitive path calls `service.getInstalled()` and then `startWatching()`, while unchanged `WorkspaceDotMcpDiscovery._watchFolder` already reads and watches the identical root file.
Findings.Title: Avoid duplicating `.mcp.json` I/O for every workspace folder
Findings.Impact: Opening a large multi-root workspace, especially over SSH/Codespaces or another remote filesystem, now bursts one additional remote file read per folder and keeps a second watcher for every root config. MCP local readiness—and therefore agent-host support assessment, which awaits `whenInitialLocalMcpServersLoaded`—cannot complete until these added scans settle; ongoing file activity also fans out through the extra listeners.
Findings.Evidence: `McpWorkbenchService` is registered eager and its constructor starts `queryLocal`; `queryLocalForGeneration` awaits `mcpManagementService.getInstalled()`, which awaits `workspaceUpdatePromise`. Initialization reaches the added flat-mapped root service for every folder. Each service's `populateLocalServers` calls `scanMcpServers`/`readFile`, and its `startWatching` installs both `fileService.watch(this.mcpResource)` and a global file-change listener. Separately, `WorkspaceDotMcpDiscovery` still calls `readFile(configFile)` and `createWatcher(configFile)` for every `.mcp.json`, so the new work duplicates an existing boundary and watcher rather than replacing it.
Findings.Recommendation: Use one owner for root-file inventory and watching: share the existing `WorkspaceDotMcpDiscovery` read/watch results with management, or make root management services lazy for write operations and subscribe them to the existing discovery updates. Preserve exact resource identity, but do not eagerly issue and retain a second read/watch pair per folder.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup and initial MCP inventory in a multi-root workspace
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The eager `McpWorkbenchService` starts `queryLocal()`, which awaits `IWorkbenchMcpManagementService.getInstalled()`, the workspace `workspaceUpdatePromise`, and every initial resource service scan. The newly added root scans therefore block `whenInitialLocalMcpServersLoaded`; agent-host MCP support explicitly awaits that promise before completing its assessment.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read each folder's `.mcp.json` through `scanMcpServers` during eager management initialization
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One newly introduced read attempt per workspace folder; all F are launched in the same initial batch. Existing discovery separately performs another root read per folder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Management scanned only the workspace and each folder's `.vscode/mcp.json`; root reads occurred independently in after-restore discovery rather than on management readiness.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The new reads must settle before workspace management `getInstalled()` and `whenInitialLocalMcpServersLoaded` complete; remote filesystem latency therefore extends MCP readiness.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Retain an uncorrelated file-provider watch and global file-change listener for every root resource
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One newly introduced watch/listener per workspace folder for process lifetime, while `WorkspaceDotMcpDiscovery` already owns a correlated watch for the same root file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only `WorkspaceDotMcpDiscovery` watched each `.mcp.json`; workspace management watched legacy resources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Watch setup follows each initial scan; retained watchers and listeners add ongoing provider, memory, IPC, and event-dispatch cost rather than only one-time startup work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: F open workspace folders. The effective added cardinality is one root `readFile` attempt and one retained root management watch/listener per folder, including folders without `.mcp.json`; this is in addition to the existing root discovery read/watch.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Initialization uses one `Promise.allSettled` over both legacy and root services for all added folders, with no limiter, so the added F root reads/watch registrations can burst concurrently. Workspace-folder change batches are serialized through `workspaceUpdatePromise`, but operations within each batch are not limited.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each management service memoizes only completion of its own initialization; there is no shared content or negative cache between management and `WorkspaceDotMcpDiscovery`. Missing root files are still read and watched once by each owner. Later changes are independently re-read by both owners after separate schedulers.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the eager await chain, per-folder flat-map, unconditional scan/watch lifecycle, and independent pre-existing discovery watcher are all explicit in code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical folder counts and remote provider latency vary, but large multi-root workspaces are realistic and the exact F-wide added boundary fan-out is deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: the PR puts a duplicate per-folder root read on MCP readiness and retains a second root watcher/listener for the workspace lifetime.

Scenarios.Scenario: Editing an existing workspace-root `.mcp.json` and refreshing runtime/workbench state
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The file save itself does not await MCP refresh. Afterward, both root discovery and the new management service independently process the change; runtime availability waits for discovery's 500 ms scheduler, while workbench metadata uses management's 50 ms scheduler.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the changed `.mcp.json` independently in discovery and management
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two reads for one changed root resource after this PR: one pre-existing discovery read and one introduced management read, after their independent debounce windows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only root discovery read and rebuilt runtime definitions for root-file edits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the editor save critical path, but on the path to refreshed runtime and workbench MCP state; repeated edits repeat both reads.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One changed root file containing S server entries; across active folders, retained listener dispatch scales with F, while parsing/normalization scales with S for the affected file.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each owner coalesces its own events with a `RunOnceScheduler`, but there is no coalescing across discovery and management. Their reads can overlap; discovery rejects stale sequences, while management's scheduler does not share that sequence.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Neither owner shares a warm content cache. Every accepted change causes each path to read and parse the file again; management reconstructs all S local records, while discovery reconstructs all S definitions.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for duplicated reads and independent scheduling; user-visible duration depends on provider and file size.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Root files are usually small and edits relatively infrequent, so the per-edit CPU portion alone is minor; the retained per-folder listener/watch fan-out is the stronger concern.
Scenarios.Verdict: Covered by the reported duplicate-owner finding; no separate finding because it has the same causal mechanism and fix.

Scenarios.Scenario: Manually adding or removing one MCP server in a workspace folder
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Destination selection may first test the legacy file; root persistence then enters a per-resource queue, reads/parses the root, validates concurrent modification, writes/creates it, and refreshes local state before the command returns and starts the discovered server.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve whether the legacy configuration exists before choosing a destination
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one resolve for the selected folder when root mode is enabled and the server is root-compatible.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Manual workspace additions wrote directly to the legacy target without this existence check.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks presentation of the destination/default choice, but is bounded to one resource and required to preserve the specified routing behavior.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and create/write the selected root configuration, including conflict validation
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Missing file: one failed read plus one create. Existing changed file: initial read, validation read, then one write. Follow-up local refresh reads once more through management.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Root installation was unsupported; legacy installation used the existing profile scanner/read-write path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These serial operations are on the user-command critical path, but they are bounded to one selected resource and provide persistence/concurrency semantics.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected folder and one server per user action. File parse/edit cost scales with the selected configuration's bytes and S entries, not all workspace folders.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Updates to the same canonical resource are serialized by `getResourceAccessQueue`. Different resources can proceed concurrently. Existing-file writes perform a serial second read for conflict detection before write.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No persistent content cache; each operation reads current contents. The second read on update intentionally verifies content and supplies current etag/mtime. Missing files use create-without-overwrite semantics.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the boundary sequence and queueing behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote filesystem latency can make the bounded sequence noticeable, but the cardinality is fixed per explicit user action.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the bounded I/O implements destination selection and conflict-safe persistence, with same-resource serialization preventing a write burst.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command resolves root and legacy existence in parallel, optionally presents a picker, then opens the selected editor. The editor open waits until both existence checks settle.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two parallel resolves per invocation, followed by the normal editor read for the selected file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The command opened `.vscode/mcp.json` directly and left file resolution to the editor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The maximum of the two resolve latencies precedes editor opening, but this is bounded and required to decide whether to open directly or show the dual-file picker.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Exactly two candidate resources for one selected folder, independent of total workspace-folder count after the folder itself is chosen.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The two `resolve` operations run concurrently with `Promise.all`; there is no broader fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No explicit cache; each command invocation rechecks both resources so the picker reflects current filesystem state.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A slow remote provider can make the added wait visible, but it remains two parallel calls on an explicit command.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: bounded parallel checks are intrinsic to the new open-the-existing-file behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: Gallery/raw-URI installation and post-install server startup
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Gallery resolution/install retains its prior network and persistence paths. The changed post-install lookup now uses the installed server's exact ID; waiting uses an autorun with a five-second timeout and starts the matching runtime server once discovered.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve/install gallery MCP metadata and later synchronize installed non-root names
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One batched request over deduplicated non-root names when synchronization is scheduled; root servers are filtered before the boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same gallery network paths existed; the diff narrows matching and excludes independently discovered root entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Install resolution is on the explicit installation path; background registry sync is not on server startup's direct critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One installation and scans over currently known runtime servers/collections; no new per-gallery-item network fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The autorun is reactive and self-disposes on a match or timeout. Gallery synchronization remains one batched resolve over deduplicated non-root installed names.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Gallery source generations and registry synchronization behavior are retained; root-format servers are explicitly excluded from gallery resolution. No new cache key or negative-cache loop was found.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Registry latency varies, but no changed call cardinality tied to root servers remains after filtering.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: exact-ID matching and root exclusion do not add expensive boundary work, and the observer cleanup remains bounded.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 24 changed files and relevant transitive startup, discovery, persistence, watcher, gallery, and agent-host paths. Submitted one medium-confidence-high finding for the newly duplicated per-folder root scan/watch lifecycle; other new I/O is bounded to explicit commands or required persistence semantics.
